attempted_claim: Let Q_n be a uniform quadrangulation with simple boundary with n faces, with three marked boundary points dividing the boundary into three arcs, and equip it with critical face percolation (open with probability 3/4). Define the quadrangulation Cardy embedding of an interior face v by the triple of crossing probabilities that v connects to each boundary arc, and let v_n be a uniformly sampled interior face. Prove or disprove that the Cardy coordinate of v_n converges in law to the continuum Cardy map (the explicit conformal map to the triangle given by Cardy-Rs formula) applied to a Brownian-disk mass-sampled point, and in particular that for fixed boundary arcs the discrete crossing probability converges to the continuum Cardy formula value. A complete answer is either a rigorous proof of this single-point Cardy-embedding convergence and crossing-probability limit for quadrangulations, or a rigorous disproof exhibiting a different limit function, a different limit law, or failure of convergence.
decisive_failure: The single permitted literature-recovery call failed mechanically, so the exact half-plane quadrangulation percolation threshold and the existence of a quadrangulation percolation to SLE6/Cardy theorem could not be verified externally; all threshold remarks above remain heuristic and no auditable emergent result is claimed.
